method: Ranked by claude-sonnet-5-5, which read 14 of 14 shortlisted pieces

picks.title: Talking Venice with Mahesh Subramony at AMD In-Depth
picks.author: George Cozma
picks.why_it_matters: AMD's server architect explains why Venice moved to 2.5D packaging, split the I/O die, and added a spare 33rd core, with power, yield, and cost reasoning.

picks.title: What does it mean to understand what we built?
picks.author: marcbrooker@gmail.com (Marc Brooker)
picks.why_it_matters: Argues that software understanding should shift from code to as-built system properties, asking for Bode-plot-style tools for emergent behavior like metastable failures.

picks.title: Robot swarms trained by trial and error in simulation keep working on real robots
picks.author: IRIDIA
picks.why_it_matters: Treats the sim-to-real gap as overfitting: limiting RL to switching among fixed behaviors transfers reliably to 20 real robots, and simpler policies beat flexible ones.

picks.title: J.R.R. Tolkien on Fairy Tales, Language, the Psychology of Fantasy, and Why There’s No Such Thing as Writing “For Children”
picks.author: Maria Popova
picks.why_it_matters: Tolkien's 1939 argument that fairy tales aren't inherently for children, with adjectives as the root of magic and humans as sub-creators.

picks.title: How to Make the Ink Used to Write Hamlet, the Declaration of Independence, and Beethoven’s Fifth
picks.author: Simon Garfield
picks.why_it_matters: The chemistry and business history of iron gall and Stephens' blue-black ink, from oak galls and a 1483 recipe to a Keats-linked surgeon's industrial formula.
